lines.text: Let me begin with a person, not a theory.
Aarav is seventeen. He lives in a crowded neighbourhood in contemporary India. He is good at mathematics. He likes pulling apart broken gadgets and figuring out how they work.
It is not an extraordinary dream. But a dream is two things: something you want, and something you believe might be possible.
First, let us see how we manage the next few months.
Nobody bans Aarav from studying. The household simply needs income now. His father's work is irregular. Coaching costs money.
Time runs out before the day does.
Aarav starts helping at Sharma uncle's electronics repair shop. He still studies at night. Then less. Then not at all.
This story is about what happens next — not to his career, but to his desire.
